_metadata.title: Cluevoyance Unlimited - 20-word pair-clue pilot
_metadata.clue_text_rule: Single uppercase word. The game does not enforce a word count in code (EditableClueTab only trims and uppercases), but all 24 clues authored in the existing game are single words of 4-5 letters, and the left/right clue tabs render vertically. One-word clues are therefore used throughout this pilot.

clues.explanation: A bridge spans the river from one bank to the other.
You cross a bridge to reach the far bank.
Bridge is a card game and the banker is the role that handles the money in card games.
Crowns are made of gold and gold is what banks were built to hold.
The crown is royalty and Royal Bank is one of the commonest bank names there is.
The Royal Mint belongs to the crown and strikes the coins the banks hand out.
Diamonds are kept in a bank vault.
The diamond heist and the bank job are the same film plot.
A diamond goes in a safe and the safe goes in a bank.
A plane banks into a turn on the power of its engines.
To bank is to turn on an angle and the engine is what drives the turn.
A bank has a drive-through window and an engine is the thing that drives.
A fire alarm and a bank alarm are both standard emergency fixtures.
A firebreak stops a blaze spreading, and to break the bank means to spend everything.
Banks keep valuables in safes, and those safes are specifically built to be fireproof.
A ghost vanishes and so does money that disappears from a bank account.
A ghost is an empty shell of a person and an empty account is a bank balance at zero.
A ghost town with its abandoned bank and open vault is the stock Western image.
A blood bank stores the blood the heart pumps.
You steal from a bank and you steal someone's heart.
A trust is a banking arrangement and trust is a matter of the heart.
Bees store honey for the winter exactly as a bank stores money.
A honey pot holds the honey and a pot of money is what you bank.
A hive is where bees bank the honey they have collected.
A stable is where a horse is kept and a bank is supposed to be financially stable.
A horse charges into battle and bank charges are the fees on your account.
You bet on a horse and you bank on a sure thing; both are staking money on an outcome.
Banks hold gold bars and iron bars are what keep a vault shut.
A bank vault is defined by its heavy iron door.
A bank safe is a box of thick iron.
A bank vault is the thing a key is needed for.
A bank locks its money away and a key is what opens a lock.
A safe deposit box sits in a bank and opens with the customer's own key.
A floodlight is a lamp and a flood is what happens when a river bursts its banks.
A bank of switches is the term for a row of them, and switches are what turn lights on.
A green light means go and greenbacks are the money a bank holds.
Still water along a bank reflects the sky the way a mirror does.
The water held by the banks acts as a mirror when it is calm.
A mirror image is the reflection and a bank's public image is what it spends fortunes protecting.
The moon is described as silver, and silver is the metal money banks were built on.
A bank has a vault, and the vault of heaven is the old phrase for the night sky the moon crosses.
Banks have a night deposit box, and night is when the moon is out.
A grassy bank is planted up as a garden and the rose is the garden flower.
A rose bed is where they are planted and a river bed sits between the banks.
A rose bursts into bloom and a river bursts its banks.
Roman soldiers were paid in salt, which is where the word salary comes from, and salary is what goes into the bank.
A bank holds cash reserves and salt was stockpiled in reserves as a vital commodity.
Worth your salt is the idiom and net worth is the figure the bank cares about.
Trees along a river bank throw their shadows across the water.
Shade is another word for shadow and a shady bank is where you sit on a hot day.
A shadow is a patch of dark and dark money is what moves through the shadow banking system.
A river runs between its banks and a snake is what basks along them.
To snake means to wind along, which is exactly what a river does between its banks.
A snake basks in the sun on a warm bank.
Spring break is the holiday and breaking the bank is the idiom for overspending.
A spring is where water comes out of the ground and a bank is what water runs between.
A spring feeds the river and the river runs between its banks.
A crown and a bridge are both things a dentist fits in your mouth.
A crown caps one tooth and a bridge spans the gap where others are missing.
London Bridge is the famous crossing and the crown jewels sit a few hundred yards away.
Diamonds is a card suit and bridge is a card game.
In bridge a suit is named as trumps and diamonds is one of the four that can be.
Both belong to the same deck of fifty-two.
A ship has a bridge where the captain stands and an engine room below decks.
A railway bridge is built for the engine to cross.
Iron bridges and steam engines were both held together with rivets.
To burn your bridges is the idiom, and burning is what fire does.
London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme and the Great Fire of London is the city's other famous story.
Fire weakens a structure until it collapses, and a collapsing bridge is the classic disaster image.
A toll is what you pay to cross a bridge and a bell tolls for the dead.
You cross a bridge to get over the water, and the old belief is that a ghost cannot cross running water at all.
Mist hangs on a river bridge and a figure in the mist is how the story always starts.
Hearts is a card suit and bridge is a card game.
Cross my heart is the promise and crossing is what a bridge is for.
A bridge closes a gap and a hole in the heart is a gap surgeons close.
The Golden Gate is the famous bridge and honey is golden.
Niagara Falls is the honeymoon capital and the crossing there was actually named the Honeymoon Bridge.
Honeycomb is the hexagonal structure bees build and honeycomb panels are used as decking in real bridges because the shape is so strong.
A horse is led across the bridge.
The bridge of the nose is the bony ridge and a horse's nose is the most recognisable part of it.
Hooves trotting over the boards is the sound a wooden bridge makes.
A bridge is built out of iron girders.
Iron bridges are held together by thousands of rivets.
An iron bridge rusts, which is why they are forever being repainted.
A song has a bridge in the middle and is written in a key.
A piano has keys at the front and the strings inside pass over a bridge.
A note is sounded by pressing a key and carried by the bridge of a stringed instrument.
A rainbow is made of light and in Norse myth it is the bridge to Asgard.
A bridge is lined with lamps so it can be crossed at night.
Tower Bridge is the famous crossing and a lighthouse is a tower built to hold a light.
Still water under a bridge works as a mirror.
A bridge reflects in the river below it.
An arch and its reflection make a double, which is the only thing a mirror ever gives you.
A bridge arches over the water and the moon arcs across the sky.
A bridge exists to be crossed and the moon crosses the sky each night.
A Japanese moon bridge is arched so steeply that its reflection completes a full circle like a full moon.
A rose arch is a garden structure and an arch is what holds a bridge up.
Monet painted the same rose-covered Japanese bridge in his garden over and over.
A climbing rose goes up the trellis and climbers go over the bridge.
A bridge ices over before the road does, which is why the salt lorry goes across it first.
Road salt is what rots the steel in a bridge.
Grit and salt are what get spread across a bridge in winter.
The troll lives under the bridge in its shadow.
A bridge arch throws a black shadow on the water below.
Under the bridge is where the shadow is and where people shelter.
A river snakes across the country and a bridge is what gets you over it.
The cables slung across a suspension bridge hang in long snaking curves.
You cross a bridge and a snake crossing the path is what stops you dead.
A suspension bridge hangs from cables and a car's suspension rides on springs.
A bridge crosses water and a spring is where that water starts.
A long bridge bounces underfoot the way a spring does.
The crown jewels are diamonds.
A diamond is set into the band of a crown.
A crown sparkles because of the diamonds in it.
A crown is political power and an engine is mechanical power.
The royal train carries the crown and is pulled by an engine.
The crown wheel is a real gear inside a car's drivetrain.
Crowns are made of gold and firelight is a golden colour.
Ring of Fire is a familiar name, and a crown is a ring worn on the head.
Crown jewels are the obvious link, and fire is the gemmologist's term for the flashes of colour inside a cut stone.
Hamlet opens with the ghost of a king demanding his stolen crown be avenged.
A king wears the crown and the ghost of a dead king is the oldest story there is.
The castle is where the crown lives and where its ghosts are said to walk.
The Queen of Hearts is the card and a queen is who wears the crown.
The King of Hearts is in every deck and a king is crowned.
Hearts is a card suit and the crowned royals are the face cards.
The queen bee rules the hive that makes the honey and a queen is who wears the crown.
Honey is gold in a jar and a crown is gold on a head.
Honeycomb holds the honey and an ornamental comb is worn in the hair like a small crown.
The Triple Crown is the prize a horse wins by taking all three of the great races.
The crown is royalty and royal horses draw the coronation coach.
The crowned monarch rides in a carriage pulled by horses.
The Iron Throne is the seat and the crown is what goes with it.
A king wears the crown and the Iron Crown of Lombardy is the one medieval kings were given.
A crown is worked metal and iron is the commonest metal there is.
The keys to the kingdom is the phrase and the crown is what rules the kingdom.
The crown jewels are kept under lock and key.
The crown jewels are locked in the Tower of London and only a keyholder gets in.
The Statue of Liberty wears a spiked crown and holds up a torch of light.
A halo is a ring of light that sits exactly where a crown would.
A crown is gold and golden light is the warm kind.
The wicked queen wears the crown and asks the mirror on the wall who is fairest.
A vanity is the table with the mirror and vanity is the sin a crown encourages.
A gilt mirror frame and a crown are both gold.
A halo ring often appears around the moon, and a crown is a ring that sits above the head the same way.
A queen wears the crown, and the moon is traditionally a queen or goddess in mythology.
A crown is a ring for the head and a ring of light circles the moon on hazy nights.
A crown of thorns is the famous one and thorns are what a rose is armed with.
The Tudor rose is the emblem of the English crown.
A garland of roses worn on the head is a crown in all but name.
A crown caps a tooth and a salt-water rinse is what the dentist sends you home with.
To sit above the salt meant sitting at the top of the table near the crowned head.
The salt tax was one of the crown's great sources of revenue.
A crown sits on the head and the head is what casts the shadow.
The crown of a tree is its canopy, and the canopy is what throws the shade.
The heir spends a lifetime waiting in the shadow of the crown.
Egyptian pharaohs wore a rearing cobra on the front of the crown.
The Egyptian crown carried a serpent and the snake was a royal emblem there.
A cobra's hood flares out around its head exactly where a crown would sit.
A flower crown is what is worn at spring festivals.
The May Queen is crowned to mark the arrival of spring.
The crown of a tree is its top, and in spring that crown comes into leaf.
A diamond is pure carbon and carbon is what builds up inside a dirty engine.
Diamonds are made by pressure and an engine runs on compressing everything in the cylinder.
Diamond-tipped tools are what machine engine parts to size.
A diamond is pure carbon, and carbon is what burns in a fire.
Diamonds sparkle and fires throw sparks.
Diamonds form under intense heat, and heat is what fire produces.
The Hope Diamond is supposed to be cursed and to have haunted everyone who owned it.
A colourless diamond is called pale and so is a ghost.
A stolen diamond vanishes overnight and so does a ghost.
Hearts and diamonds are the two red suits in a deck of cards.
Both suits are printed in red.
A diamond ring is what you offer along with your heart.
You put a diamond ring on the finger of the person you call honey.
Clarity is how a diamond is graded and clear runny honey is the other kind.
A diamond is cut by a jeweller and cheap honey is cut with syrup.
A carrot is what you hold out to a horse and a carat is what a diamond is weighed in.
A show horse is paraded in the ring and a diamond is set in one.
A winning horse and a flawless diamond are both described as a prize.
A diamond is the hardest thing there is and iron is the byword for hard.
A diamond-tipped blade is the thing that cuts hardened iron.
Iron and diamonds are both dug out of mines.
A key is cut at the hardware shop and a diamond is cut by a jeweller.
A diamond goes in the safe and a key is what opens it.
Diamonds are kept under lock and a key is what turns it.
A diamond sparkles because of what it does to the light passing through it.
A diamond works as a prism, splitting light into colours.
The cut of a diamond is chosen entirely to control how light leaves it.
A diamond shines and shining is what light does.
A diamond is the one thing that will scratch glass, which is what a mirror is.
A mirror is silvered glass and a fake diamond is glass pretending.
A mirror is cut to size and a diamond is cut to sparkle.
A diamond ring is the classic object, and a ring of light circles the moon.
Diamonds shine and so does the moon.
Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds puts both the diamonds and the night sky's moon in one image.
The rose cut is a genuine antique style of cutting a diamond.
A dozen roses and a diamond ring are two ways of saying the same thing.
A pink diamond is the rarest kind and pink is the colour of a rose.
Salt and diamond are both crystals, one you can grow on a string and one you cannot.
Salt and diamonds are both dug out of mines.
Salt is white and a colourless diamond is called white too.
A black diamond is a real stone and a shadow is black.
A flaw inside a diamond shows up as a dark shadow in the stone.
A diamond is entirely about light and a shadow is where light is not.
A diamondback is a rattlesnake, named for the diamonds running down its back.
A snake's skin is patterned in diamonds.
Snake scales are diamond-shaped and overlap like a cut stone's facets.
A baseball diamond is the infield and spring training is when the season starts.
April is the heart of spring and the diamond is April's birthstone.
A diamond ring is for the proposal and spring is the classic wedding season.
An engine burns fuel and burning is what fire is.
Fire engines are painted red and flames are red.
A steam engine works by using fire to boil water.
The ghost in the machine is the phrase for a mind inside a mechanism, and an engine is the machine meant.
The ghost train is the fairground ride and a train is pulled by an engine.
The Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost is one of the most famous engines ever built.
The heart is a pump and an engine runs on pumping pistons.
A stalled engine and a stopped heart are both jump-started.
A motor is an engine and the heart is the motor that keeps a body going.
Honey is sweet and a mechanic will tell you a well-tuned engine runs sweet.
Honey is thick and so is the oil an engine runs on.
Engine oil and honey pour with exactly the same slow reluctance.
Horsepower is the unit an engine is still measured in.
The iron horse was the name given to the first steam engines.
The car was first called a horseless carriage because the engine had replaced the horse.
An engine block is cast iron.
A steam engine is several tons of iron.
The train's engine is the iron horse.
The ignition key is what fires the engine.
A key is what starts an engine.
You turn the key and the engine turns over.
A spark plug fires the engine and a spark is a flash of light.
The engine warning light is the one nobody wants on the dashboard.
A car is an engine with lights on the front.
A car is an engine with mirrors bolted to it.
A show engine is polished chrome and so is a mirror's frame.
A mirror is polished to see yourself in and an engine is polished for the same vanity.
A rocket engine is the only thing that has ever carried anyone to the moon.
The Apollo programme reached the moon on the strength of the Saturn V's engines.
Engines launch the craft, and the moon was the destination of the most famous launches.
Steam rose off the engine, and rose is the past tense of rise.
Rose oil goes in perfume and engine oil goes in the sump.
Rose is the heroine of Titanic and the ship's engine room is one of the film's set pieces.
Land speed records are set on the Bonneville Salt Flats by engines built for nothing else.
Road salt eats the underside of a car and everything the engine sits in.
A ship's engine spends its life fighting salt air.
An engine block is the main casting and a block of shadow is what a tall building throws.
A great engine looms over you and so does a shadow.
A steam engine drags its long shadow across open country behind it.
A snake hisses and so does an engine letting off steam or air.
A snake coils and an engine fires through its ignition coil.
The hoses coiled under a car bonnet look exactly like snakes.
An engine's valves are held shut by valve springs.
An engine fires through its ignition coil and a spring is a coil of wire.
Clockwork is an engine driven entirely by a wound spring.
Ghost stories are traditionally told around a campfire.
A ghost is a spirit, and spirits are the flammable drinks that catch fire.
Smoke rises from fire and drifts in exactly the pale, insubstantial way ghosts are pictured.
Fire burns, and heartburn is the familiar complaint.
Passion is described as fiery, and the heart is its traditional seat.
A fire keeps you warm and warm-hearted describes a kind person.
Smoke comes from fire, and beekeepers use smoke to calm the hive before taking honey.
Honey is golden and so is firelight.
Bees make honey, and a beekeeper's smoker is a small fire carried to the hive.
A wildfire and a wild horse both take the same modifier.
Horses are marked with a brand, and the branding iron is heated in a fire.
The Trojan horse led to Troy being sacked and burned.
Iron is shaped in a forge, which is a contained fire.
Fire is hot, and the saying is to strike while the iron is hot.
A branding iron is heated in a fire before it is used.
A blacksmith works iron using fire.
The ignition key is turned to fire the engine.
A fire escape gets you out of a building and a key gets you out of a locked room.
You start a fire, and a key is what starts a car.
A match starts a fire and is struck to make light.
A candle is a small contained fire kept specifically for its light.
A torch is a burning brand and also the everyday word for a hand-held light.
A spark is a flash of light and the thing that sets a fire going.
Smoke and mirrors is the phrase for deception, and smoke comes from fire.
A mirror is glass, and glass is made by melting sand in intense fire.
A curved mirror focusing sunlight will burn and start a fire, the trick attributed to Archimedes.
Both give off a visible glow in the dark.
A campfire and the moon are both fixtures of a night-time scene.
Ring of Fire is a well-known name, and a ring or halo often appears around the moon.
The classic rose and the colour of flame are both red.
Smoke and flames rise, and rose is the past tense of rise.
Red roses are the symbol of passion and passion is described as fiery.
Curing meat is done by salting it or by smoking it over a fire.
Meat is preserved with salt and cooked over fire.
Rubbing salt in the wound and adding fuel to the fire are both idioms for making things worse.
Firelight flickers, which makes the shadows it casts flicker too.
In Plato's cave a fire behind the prisoners casts the shadows they mistake for reality.
Flames are said to dance, and so are the shadows they throw on a wall.
A dragon is a giant serpent that breathes fire.
Flames are called tongues of fire, and a snake has a famous forked tongue.
A fire hisses as it burns and a snake hisses in warning.
A hot spring is a natural feature, and fire is the definition of hot.
Spring is the season that warms up, and a fire is what you sit beside to get warm.
Flames leap upward, and to spring is to leap.
A ghost is a spirit and the heart is where spirit in the sense of courage is said to live.
A ghost haunts a house and a regret haunts the heart.
The heart stops and that is the moment a person gives up the ghost.
Telling the bees is the old custom of going out to the hive to inform it when someone in the house has died.
A honeytrap is the lure and a ghost trap is what Ghostbusters carry.
Honey is kept in a jar and a trapped spirit in a jar is a staple of folk magic.
The Headless Horseman is a ghost on horseback.
Behold a pale horse, and the name of the one who sat on it was Death.
The phantom rider on his horse is the oldest shape a ghost story takes.
Marley's ghost drags iron chains the length of A Christmas Carol.
Cold iron is the traditional folk charm against ghosts and spirits.
The haunted castle with its iron gates is the setting every ghost story wants.
A key is what you need for a locked door and a ghost simply walks through it.
A key opens the door and a ghost is what comes through it anyway.
The haunted house is handed over with one big rusted key.
Lights flickering is the standard film signal that a ghost has arrived.
Ghost hunters photograph floating orbs of light and call them spirits.
A ghost is pale and pale light is the weak kind.
Bloody Mary is the game where you say the name into a mirror until something appears behind you.
A ghost is the thing you see reflected over your shoulder that is not in the room.
Mirrors are covered in a house of mourning so the spirit does not get caught in one.
A ghost is pale and so is the moon.
Ghosts walk at night and the moon is what lights it.
Ghosts haunt, and a full moon is the standard backdrop for a haunting.
Roses are laid on a grave and a ghost is what rises from one.
The smell of roses with no roses in the room is a stock sign of a haunting.
A white rose and a white figure on the stairs.
A circle of salt is the traditional protection against a ghost crossing into a room.
You throw spilled salt over your shoulder to keep the bad spirits off.
Spilling salt is the old omen, and what it is supposed to summon is nothing good.
A shadowy figure is the exact phrase people reach for when they think they have seen a ghost.
Ghosts haunt a house and shadows haunt its corners.
Both belong to the dark and neither is solid.
A shed snakeskin is left behind as an empty, transparent ghost of the animal.
A snake leaves its whole skin behind and what is left looks like an apparition of it.
A snake glides without a sound and so does a ghost.
In spring everything rises out of the ground and a ghost is something that rises from the grave.
Spring-heeled Jack was the Victorian phantom, and a jack-in-the-box is the toy on a spring.
A ghost sends a chill down your spine and an early spring morning still carries a chill.
Sweetheart is the word and honey is the definition of sweet.
Honey is what you call someone you love and the heart is love's symbol.
Honey, darling and sweetheart are the same pet name three times over.
Horses race and your heart races when you are frightened.
A heart beats and hooves beat the ground.
A horse gallops and a galloping heart is one going far too fast.
Blood is red because of the iron in it and the heart is what pumps it round.
Iron is cold to the touch and a cold heart is one with no feeling in it.
The heart is a pump and the old village pump was a lump of cast iron.
A key unlocks a door and the phrase is unlocking someone's heart.
A locket is heart-shaped and named for the lock a key would open.
A heart pendant and a key are both worn on a chain round the neck.
In Egyptian myth the heart is weighed against a feather, and light as a feather is the phrase for weighing nothing.
Light of my life is the endearment and the heart is love's symbol.
Warm light and a warm heart are both about comfort.
A broken heart and a broken mirror are both bad news, one of them for seven years.
The eyes are called the mirror of the soul and the heart is where the soul is said to sit.
A mirror reflects an image and to reflect is to search your own heart.
The heart is the symbol of love and moonlight is its traditional setting.
A full moon is the striking phase, and a full heart means being overwhelmed with feeling.
To pine is to ache with longing, which is both a matter of the heart and what mooning over someone means.
Red roses and paper hearts are the two images of Valentine's Day.
A red rose and a heart are the two standard symbols of love.
The classic rose and the drawn heart are both red.
Tears are salt water and heartbreak is what brings them.
Salt raises blood pressure, which is what puts the heart under strain.
Salt of the earth is what you call someone with a good heart.
A dark heart is a wicked one and a shadow is a patch of dark.
You hide what you feel in your heart and things hide in shadow.
A secret is kept in the heart and lives in the shadows.
A snake is cold-blooded and a villain is cold-hearted.
The heart pumps blood and a snake is the famous cold-blooded animal.
A snake charmer works with a flute and a charmer works their way into your heart.
Your heart leaps with joy and to spring is to leap.
Spring is the season love is said to belong to and the heart is love's symbol.
Spring fever is the restless, lovesick feeling, which is a complaint of the heart.
A currycomb grooms the horse and honeycomb holds the honey.
Oats are what a horse is fed and honey is what goes on yours.
A horse will do anything for something sweet and honey is sweetness itself.
An iron pot hangs over the fire and a honey pot sits on the table.
A honey glaze is cooked onto meat in a cast iron pan.
Iron in the diet is taken for strength and honey is eaten for quick energy.
Honey is sticky and sticky keys are the classic complaint about a piano or a keyboard.
Honey comes from a bee and B is a musical key.
Honey is gold in the jar and a gold key is the ceremonial kind.
Honey is golden and golden light is the late afternoon kind.
Honey is amber-coloured and amber is one of the three traffic lights.
A jar of honey glows when you hold it up to the light.
Honey pours smooth and a mirror is the smoothest surface in the house.
Honey is gold in the jar and an old mirror sits in a gilt frame.
Honey goes into a face mask and the mirror is where the result gets inspected.
The honeymoon follows the wedding and is named for the moon-month of sweetness after it.
Honey is golden and a harvest moon hangs gold on the horizon.
Moon is the old root of month, and the honeymoon was originally the first month of marriage.
Bees work the roses and honey is what comes of it.
A rose holds nectar and nectar is what becomes honey.
Honey is sweet and a rose is the sweetest thing in the garden to smell.
Honey is sweetness itself and salt is its exact opposite on the tongue.
Salt cures meat and honey is the other preservative that never spoils.
Salt and sweet are two of the basic tastes and honey is the sweet one.
Dark honey is the strong-tasting kind and a shadow is a patch of dark.
The sun makes the flowers the bees need for honey and the sun is also what makes shadows.
Honey is warm gold and shadow is the absence of exactly that.
Honeyed words come off the tongue and a forked tongue is what a snake is trusted with; both describe sweet talk you should not believe.
A honeytrap is something sweet with a snake inside it.
A snake charmer does the charming and honeyed charm is how a smooth talker works.
Bees come out in spring and the honey follows.
Spring blossom is the source of the nectar that becomes honey.
Spring is pollen season and pollen is what bees carry home alongside the nectar.
A horseshoe is a bent bar of iron.
The blacksmith works iron and shoes the horses.
The iron horse was what they called the steam train when it first appeared.
A horse bolts across the field and a bolt is the lock a key throws.
The stable holds the horses and the key hangs by its door.
Locking the gate after the horse has bolted is the proverb about acting too late.
A dark horse is the unexpected winner and dark is the opposite of light.
Light horse is the historical name for light cavalry.
Light travels at the fastest speed there is and a horse is judged on nothing but speed.
You groom a horse in the stable and you groom yourself in the mirror.
A horse shies from its own reflection because it does not know what a mirror is.
The knight in chess is a horse and the White Knight rides through the looking-glass.
A mare is a female horse, and the dark plains on the moon are called maria, from mare.
A horseshoe is a crescent, which is exactly the shape of the moon in its thin phase.
A white horse and a white moon are both stock images.
The Kentucky Derby is a horse race known as the Run for the Roses.
The winning horse is draped in a blanket of roses.
A rider rises to the trot and rose is the past tense of rise.
A salt lick is the block put out in the field for horses.
A worked horse sweats and dries white with salt.
You can lead a horse to water but not make it drink, and salt water is the kind nothing can drink.
A horse shies at its own shadow on the road.
A shadow is exactly what spooks a horse.
The rider's shadow is thrown along the ground beside the horse.
Antivenom for snake bites is produced in horses, which are injected to make the serum.
A startled horse rears up and so does a cobra.
A horse is known for its tail and a snake is very nearly all tail.
The Derby is the great horse race and it is run in spring.
Foals are born in spring.
A horse jumps the fence and to spring is to jump.
A heavy iron lock is what an old key was cut for.
A locksmith cuts keys and a blacksmith works iron.
A key is a small piece of shaped metal and iron is what the old ones were cast from.
Cast iron is the material and light is cast across a room.
Iron is the byword for heavy and light is its exact opposite.
Polished iron shines when the light hits it.
A mirror is polished to a shine and iron is polished to keep the rust off.
Polished iron shines enough to see yourself in, which is how the first mirrors worked.
A mirror hangs in a wrought iron frame.
The man in the moon and Iron Man are both familiar figures.
The moon's surface and raw iron are both grey.
The moon has a small iron core, and iron is the metal we associate with a planet's core.
A wrought iron gate with roses climbing over it is the standard garden picture.
Rust is the deep red-brown of old iron and roses come in exactly that colour.
The rose garden is full of wrought iron benches and arches.
Salt is what makes iron rust.
Iron and salt are both minerals a body needs.
Sea salt eats iron, which is why ships are a losing battle.
The Iron Curtain is always described as having cast a shadow over half of Europe.
Iron bars throw striped shadows across a cell floor.
Raw iron is dark grey and a shadow is a patch of dark.
A snake coils and iron is coiled into wire and springs.
